answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with stake-bonded reputation: every identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, like a river that only flows once its channel is full. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital, not just compute. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, so an attacker loses money on every bad actor, while honest agents keep their stake and build a reputation record that stretches to the horizon of their history. The ocean of cheap identities dries up because each one must be paid for, and the cost scales linearly with the size of the attack.
